tasks.title: Dev integration proves incident preview parity and durable maintenance through the real console
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, all Behavior bullets (including revised scenario steps 6-7), Checks, Docs and Completion evidence; Required behavior 9 preview parts (message parts are p elements, with exact newlines); Acceptance evidence 1-3 and 7-8; Security impact, Rollout order 2 and Risks. After merged console, implement the independent status/preview card extractor and literal-fixture tests together with all twelve console-incidents steps. Reuse console-lib.sh req/csrf/form_token_args and password/TOTP sign-in, obtaining a later TOTP step than setup. Optional owner-directory export in console-probes.sh preserves existing callers, writes only owner email/password/TOTP key to mode-600 owner.env in mode-700 directory, and prints no credentials. Step 6 MUST open the still-open resolve page twice, save both unused form tokens and CSRF values before body replacement, preview with the first token and publish with the replacement token issued by that preview. Step 7 posts the saved second unused token (not a fresh GET after resolution), asserts 409 with exactly 4 updates/status resolved on the API, then separately asserts resolved GET 409 without form_token. Wire owner/scenario directory setup and trap cleanup around the dev-only scenario between Console probe locations and Persistence across down and up, preserving the published-full skip. Require the new exact success line alongside the two existing e2e-dev lines and run the extractor fixtures in lint. Keep parser, fixtures, auth handoff and scenario in one task because they jointly prove a single real-service integration. Update README/AGENTS and supply whole-change security, Compose and real-stack browser evidence. Apply the revised Request counting terminology: zero writes on a console preview permits its required config/incident reads. Maintenance edits use the console's stored database epochs and revision checks from section 13; do not supply original epochs in hidden fields or add any API mutation outside the console journey. Console's task file owns the per-route counter assertions of Acceptance evidence 6. Acceptance evidence 9's code-point and untitled cases are owned by console T2 and included in console T3's final evidence; this real-service scenario retains the section's specified HTML/Unicode title and literal messages. The fourth plan-review adds console-only browser round trips and automatic-detail handling; it does not alter this deploy scenario. Acceptance evidence 10 (native Chromium leading-LF and time normalization submissions) and 11 (unaddressable check ids) belong to console T2/T3. Keep the deploy comparison independent by reading the two rendered artifacts and using literal extractor fixtures, without importing console rendering or parsing code.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; independent literal fixtures from status src/render.ts:648-728 at 8b6d431 and spec section 9 produce identical JSON for title E2E Ünï 😀, impact 'Impact: major', status 'Status: investigating', affects 'Affects: Web', update investigating/message 'Line one\nLine two'. Messages preserve actual LF/Unicode exactly; head parts trim; time is excluded; < becomes < in one pass; absent/hidden affects is null; missing item exits 1. Include resolved fixtures with all 4 updates in order. Expected fixtures/JSON are literals from the named independent sources, never generated by the extractor or a console renderer. Both fixture renderings use p elements for messages as their named sources specify; an initial LF is preserved rather than being trimmed or lost through textarea/pre parsing.
exit 0; repository lint/typecheck/full CLI tests pass with the existing coverage gate; runtime dependencies and image/action pins remain unchanged

acceptance.expected: every command exits 0 from the repository root, including explicit checks of new files before they are tracked

acceptance.command: bash -o pipefail -c 'E2E_SETUP=dev bash e2e/compose-e2e.sh | tee e2e-dev.log' && grep -qx 'ok: manual incident privacy' e2e-dev.log && grep -qx 'ok: console probe locations' e2e-dev.log && grep -qx 'ok: console incidents and maintenance' e2e-dev.log
acceptance.expected: exit 0 against sibling main checkouts with the merged console child. Preview gives 200 and leaves manual-list length/maintenance revision unchanged; publication gives 303. Independently rendered real status cards equal the saved console previews after create, monitoring and resolve, excluding time only. Two open resolve GETs supply distinct usable tokens: preview uses the first, publish uses its replacement, and second unused token POST after resolve gives 409; the API retains exactly 4 updates/status resolved. A separate later GET resolve gives 409 and no name="form_token" input. Planning e2e-window gives 303; API source is database, checkIds are ['e2e-tcp','e2e-post','status-page'], start/end match the script's independently computed UTC epochs, phase planned, note E2E planned window, and status /api/maintenance lists the note for all 3 checks. checks.json SHA-256 equals the hash recorded before planning. API restart preserves the window; edit gives note E2E edited window and end+3600000 ms; delete removes it. Typed incident deletion gives 303 then API 404. Owner password/TOTP/admin token scans of console/api logs and console database files give 0 hits; owner.env/directory modes are 600/700; trap removes owner and work directories. All 3 exact success lines occur. Required console reads may occur during previews; assert unchanged API state rather than zero total API requests. Maintenance edit keeps the independently computed start epoch and changes only note and end as specified.

acceptance.command: bash -o pipefail -c 'E2E_SETUP=full bash e2e/compose-e2e.sh | tee e2e-full.log' && grep -qx 'skip: console incidents and maintenance (published images)' e2e-full.log
acceptance.expected: exit 0; published full images skip the new scenario and existing end-to-end checks still pass

acceptance.command: scripts/init-secrets.sh && docker compose -f dev/compose.yaml up -d --build && scripts/wait-ready.sh dev/compose.yaml 900
acceptance.expected: exit 0; dev stack built from sibling main checkouts with merged console is ready for the manual browser check. If Docker cannot run in the implementation environment, record the concrete reason and cite the e2e-dev CI run instead, as the spec allows

Record subsequent actual agent-browser commands and outcomes in the PR: sign in, declare with 2 components and observe live preview, publish, post identified/monitoring, resolve, reload list/MTTR/timeline and confirm later resolve 409; plan maintenance with direct checks and overlapping component, edit note/end and delete as Owner. Repeat forms at 390 px and compare real status output beside the preview, including inert HTML-looking text, Unicode and newlines. The source of expected behavior is spec sections 4-14 and status render.ts at 8b6d431; merely opening the browser is not evidence. Use only the explicitly permitted Docker-unavailable alternative when needed

acceptance.command: gh pr checks && gh pr view --json body
acceptance.expected: All required checks are green; PR names #569, reports lint/helper and Compose outcomes with ok: console incidents and maintenance, and records actual agent-browser commands/results or concrete Docker-unavailable reason with e2e-dev run. Applicable security evidence includes modes 600/700, cleanup, 0 secret hits, no credential printing, one-pass entity decoding/inert text/exact messages and unchanged dependency/image/action pins. README documents dev-only scenario/full skip; AGENTS lists helper command and third e2e-dev gate. Known limits state status markup coupling, time/container layout excluded and merged console prerequisite. Evidence covers checks 1-3 (incident journey, preview parity, maintenance), 7 (mobile) and 8 (secrets); console supplies checks 6 (per-route counts) and 9 (code-point/untitled cases). Console also supplies checks 10 (native-browser textarea/time round trips) and 11 (unaddressable automatic check ids); these do not add steps to the real-service scenario.
